result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.negative_edge_cycle()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if the graph contains a cycle of negative total weight. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L40402-L40456){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.negative_edge_cycle(weighted=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Negative edge cycle](/assets/graphs/negative-edge-cycle.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three currencies linked by exchange edges weighted with negative log-rates. Left: USD to EUR −0.10, EUR to GBP −0.15 and GBP to USD +0.20 add up to −0.05, a negative cycle (accent) that signals an arbitrage loop, so negative_edge_cycle() returns True. Right: with GBP to USD at +0.30 the loop totals +0.05, so no cycle is negative and the call returns False." width="100%"} Shortest paths are only well defined when no cycle has negative total weight; otherwise going around the cycle again always makes a route cheaper. Negative weights appear with costs that can be gains (currency exchange rates as negative log-rates, refunds, energy recovery), and a negative cycle then signals an arbitrage or modelling error. This method checks the whole graph, whatever node a cycle is reachable from. On an undirected graph every edge can be traversed both ways, so a single negative edge already forms a negative cycle (there and back). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag (an unweighted graph has no negative cycle). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if some cycle has negative total weight. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Bellman-Ford is run from all nodes at once (distance 0 everywhere, equivalent to a virtual source joined to every node, as in NetworkX); if distances still improve after $V$ rounds, a negative cycle exists. It runs in $O(VE)$ time. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three currencies whose exchange rates, as negative log-rates, admit an arbitrage loop: ::: {#8a34f40c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec fx = ec.Graph(directed=True, weighted=True).add_nodes(["USD", "EUR", "GBP"]) fx.add_edges([("USD", "EUR", -0.10), ("EUR", "GBP", -0.15), ("GBP", "USD", 0.20)]) fx.negative_edge_cycle() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: :::
